All six slots cited by the reviewer are factually present in ducklib.py and use intp where uint64 is correct per duckdb.h. Verified directly:

- ducklib.py:105  signatures["duckdb_column_count"] = intp(intp)    — duckdb.h returns idx_t (uint64_t)
- ducklib.py:155  signatures["duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count"] = intp(intp)  — idx_t return
- ducklib.py:156  signatures["duckdb_data_chunk_get_size"] = intp(intp)           — idx_t return
- ducklib.py:157  signatures["duckdb_data_chunk_get_vector"] = intp(intp, intp)   — 2nd arg is idx_t col_idx
- ducklib.py:225  signatures["duckdb_row_count"] = intp(intp)                     — idx_t return
- ducklib.py:233  signatures["duckdb_validity_row_is_valid"] = int8(intp, intp)   — 2nd arg is idx_t row

The documented convention is explicit: CLAUDE.md §"Check duckdb.h first" states 'idx_t → uint64_t → uint64'. The rest of the file uses uint64 correctly for idx_t: ducklib.py:216 duckdb_nparams = uint64(intp), :226 duckdb_rows_changed = uint64(intp), :227 duckdb_struct_type_child_count = uint64(intp); and idx_t args at :106 duckdb_column_logical_type = intp(intp, uint64), :107 duckdb_column_name = intp(intp, uint64), :187 duckdb_get_list_child = intp(intp, uint64). The inconsistency is unambiguous.

Severity low is correct. Both intp (int64) and uint64 classify as _CLASS_SCALAR in numbox/core/bindings/abi.py:64-80, so both lower to LLVM i64 via the same scalar code path in call.py:146-148. At the machine-code ABI level (x86-64 SysV, AAPCS64, Windows x64) there is zero difference: i64 is i64 regardless of signedness. Signed/unsigned reinterpretation only diverges at values >= 2^63, which is practically unreachable for row/column/chunk counts and column/row indices. There is no functional harm for real-world inputs. The only actual cost is type-system inconsistency: a caller in @njit that passes the intp return of duckdb_column_count to a second function expecting uint64 will trigger a numba implicit cast (sign-extend int64 → uint64), which is a no-op for non-negative values. Severity low is appropriate; raising it to medium would require evidence of a concrete failure mode, which does not exist.
